new_statements.relation_note: Contrastive tone universal in Cross River; mostly two levels; stress only as sentence-level focus marking.
new_statements.rule_in_words: All Cross River languages (hence Umon, an Upper Cross language) have contrastive lexical/grammatical tone interacting with downdrift, register raising and boundary pitch effects; most have two contrastive tone levels. 'Stress or accent' is mentioned only as a sentence-level focus phenomenon that Cross River languages have grammaticalised to varying degrees -- no word-stress claim.
new_statements.exceptions: Ogoni languages (and others, text truncated) have more than two tone levels; nothing Umon-specific.
new_statements.identity_note: Family-level survey chapter on Cross River (incl. Upper Cross, where Faraclas's classification table lists 'Umon? Umon (under U6?)' in the Ubaghara-Kohumono cluster). The tone statement is a generalisation over 'all Cross River languages', not a first-hand statement about Umon; it covers Umon only by membership. Not linked to umon1238 in Glottolog; our bibliography lists it as print-only/unread. archive.org copy is controlled digital lending (borrow with account); text was reached only through archive.org full-text-search snippets of the scanned.
